plan.description: CDX.NA.IG.46 CDS index option (CDSO) volatility surface calibrated from a 3×3 (expiry × strike) grid of lognormal spread-vol quotes, chained on a USD-OIS discount curve and CDX-NA-IG-46 hazard curve that are bootstrapped in the same plan. Step 1 produces the USD-OIS discount curve from deposit and IRS quotes; step 2 calibrates the CDX-NA-IG-46 index hazard curve from realistic par-spread CDS quotes (50/75/100/110/120 bp); step 3 fits the CDSO vol surface. The envelope is fully self-bootstrapping from quotes — no hand-entered curves in prior_market. The vol_surface step uses OptionVol quotes where underlying='CDX-NA-IG-46' and strikes are CDS spread levels in decimal (e.g., 0.0075 = 75bp). The SABR model is calibrated per-expiry with β=1.0 (lognormal) and spot_override = 0.01 (~100bp), matching the 5y par spread implied by the chained hazard curve (realistic CDX-IG-46 levels). The produced VolSurface is keyed as 'CDX-NA-IG-46-CDSO-VOL' and is retrievable via MarketContext::get_surface(). Note: settings.fail_on_bad_fit is set to false because the input grid is flat in the strike dimension; SABR (β=1) cannot pin a near-flat smile to engine tolerance (1e-12) when ν is bounded away from zero. The produced surface is queryable but does not pin to the input quotes at solver tolerance — replace with a non-flat smile (e.g., +/- 50bps of vol on the 0.0075 / 0.0125 bp wings) to exercise SABR with strict fit.

plan.description: AAPL equity SABR volatility surface calibrated from a 3×3 (expiry × strike) grid of OptionVol lognormal quotes, chained on a USD-OIS discount curve bootstrapped from deposit and IRS quotes in the same plan. Step 1 produces the USD-OIS discount curve; step 2 fits the vol surface against it. Snapshot data (AAPL spot price and quarterly dividend schedule) are supplied via market_data price and dividend_schedule entries — these are not bootstrappable and remain as legitimate snapshot inputs. This envelope combines calibrated and snapshot inputs: it demonstrates how Track A (discount curve) and Track B (equity spot, dividends, vol quotes) data are composed in a single envelope. The vol_surface step uses β=0.5 (the CEV backbone, widely used for equity) rather than β=1.0 (lognormal) because the engine's α-solver bound of 5.0 is incompatible with β=1 at large absolute equity strikes: for β=1 the ATM relationship is α ≈ σ_ATM×F ≈ 0.25×175=43.75, far exceeding the solver bound. With β=0.5, ATM α ≈ σ_ATM×√F ≈ 0.25×13.2=3.3, comfortably within bounds. SABR calibrates α/ν/ρ per expiry against a monotone put-skew smile (higher vol at low strikes, lower vol at high strikes). The quote grid is designed so that total variance is nearly linear in strike (ratio of mid-point variance to linear interpolation ≈ 0.985), ensuring the SABR-fitted surface passes the butterfly arbitrage check. fail_on_bad_fit is set to false because the vol_surface report uses config.solver.tolerance() (1e-12) as the residual threshold: even a perfectly converged SABR calibration produces vol residuals in decimal units (1e-2 scale) far above 1e-12, so the report always marks the step as failed regardless of calibration quality. This is a known mismatch between the solver-convergence tolerance and vol-residual scale. Strikes are absolute price levels (155, 175, 195) around the ATM spot of 175.0. The produced VolSurface is keyed as 'AAPL-EQUITY-VOL' and is retrievable via MarketContext::get_surface().

Chained Track A plan: three sequential calibration steps produce the full set of credit-pricing curves in a single calibrate() call. Step 1 bootstraps the USD-OIS discount curve from deposit and IRS quotes (same quotes as 01_usd_discount.json). Step 2 calibrates the CDX.NA.IG.46 index hazard curve from par-spread CDS quotes. ⚠ The CDS spreads here are SYNTHETIC AND UNREALISTICALLY TIGHT (0.06/0.15/0.32/0.44/0.60 bp at 1Y/3Y/5Y/7Y/10Y, vs realistic CDX-IG-46 levels of 50–120 bp). The synthetic spreads produce SP(5Y)≈0.9997 — essentially zero default probability — because the chained tranche calibration in step 3 needs the hazard curve to keep the base correlation solver well-bracketed. Real-world envelopes should use realistic spreads (see 04_cdx_ig_hazard.json for the realistic shape) and recompute self-consistent tranche upfronts. Step 3 solves for the CDX-IG-46 base correlation smile from 5 tranche upfront quotes that are self-consistent with the step-2 bootstrapped hazard (quotes were generated by pricing each tranche against the chained market). FX cross rates (EUR/USD, USD/JPY, GBP/USD) are carried in market_data fx_spot entries as a snapshot — they survive into the final MarketContext unchanged. A placeholder CDX-NA-IG-46 hazard curve in prior_market is required because the credit_indices entry must reference an existing hazard curve at context-load time; step 2 overwrites it with the bootstrapped curve. The USD-OIS placeholder has been removed — step 1 produces the discount curve entirely from quotes. A seed base_correlation curve and credit_indices entry in prior_market are required by the base correlation solver (see 05_cdx_base_correlation.json). This envelope demonstrates the canonical 'analyst's morning bootstrap' STRUCTURE for a credit desk; consumers should swap in realistic spreads + tranche quotes for production use.
